import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# --- Data Preparation for Visualization ---
# Count the number of dogs per district and per dog gender
# We assume each row represents one dog registration.
dog_gender_district_counts = df.groupby(['KreisLang', 'SexHundLang']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)

# Calculate the total number of dogs per district to sort them
dog_gender_district_counts['TotalDogs'] = dog_gender_district_counts.sum(axis=1)

# Sort districts by the total number of dogs in descending order
dog_gender_district_counts = dog_gender_district_counts.sort_values(
    'TotalDogs', ascending=False
).drop('TotalDogs', axis=1)

# --- Visualization ---
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a stacked bar chart
# The default colors will distinguish between male and female dogs
dog_gender_district_counts.plot(
    kind='bar',
    stacked=True,
    ax=plt.gca(),
    cmap='viridis' # A perceptually uniform colormap
)

# --- Customize Plot ---
plt.title('Distribution of Dog Gender Across Zurich Districts', fontsize=16, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('District (Kreis)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=10) # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)
plt.legend(title='Dog Gender', title_fontsize='11', fontsize='10',
           bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left') # Place legend outside to prevent overlap
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7) # Add a grid for easier reading of values

# Ensure all elements fit within the figure area
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
